channel.title: Jarvis Strategies Blog
channel.description: Practical thinking on AI implementation for trades and construction companies in the Okanagan.

item.title: What Does an AI Readiness Assessment Cost?
item.description: The assessment itself is free. Here's what actually drives the cost of what comes after it, and why the number varies so much between businesses.

item.title: How Long Does AI Implementation Actually Take?
item.description: Two weeks or six: what actually determines the timeline, and why it's a scope decision, not a technology one.

item.title: AI Consultant vs. Hiring In-House: How to Decide
item.description: Before you post a job listing for an in-house AI hire, work through what the role would actually do all year. For most trades and construction businesses, the math doesn't favor it.

item.title: AI for Subcontractor Coordination: A Practical Workflow for GCs
item.description: Daily site summaries, RFI triage, and schedule impact analysis eat hours from PMs and supers every day. Here's where AI helps GCs coordinate subs, and where it shouldn't touch the relationship.

item.title: AI for Engineering Documentation: Reclaiming Engineer Time from Compliance Paperwork
item.description: One manufacturing client spent 80% of engineering time on documentation, not engineering. Here's how AI cut documentation time 30-40% without breaking the audit trail.

item.title: AI for Construction Estimating: Where It Belongs (and Where It Doesn't)
item.description: Construction estimating is six jobs stacked together. Here's which ones AI genuinely helps with, which ones it can't touch, and the workflow pattern that keeps accuracy intact.

item.title: How to Cut Construction Proposal Turnaround from Days to Hours with AI
item.description: Five RFPs a week can eat a full-time estimator's schedule. Here's the AI-assisted proposal workflow that cut turnaround from three days to 90 minutes without losing pricing judgment.

item.title: What the GVBOT AI Report Missed About BC Trades and Construction
item.description: The GVBOT AI report says 69% of BC businesses can't find an AI use case. For trades and construction, that number is misleading — here's what the survey actually missed.

item.title: AI Adoption in BC Construction: Why the Okanagan Lags Vancouver
item.description: BC construction lags every sector in AI adoption and the Okanagan trails the Lower Mainland. What the gap means for trades contractors in Vernon, Kelowna, and across the Interior.

item.title: Where AI Actually Fits in a Trades Business
item.description: Most AI tools are built for tech companies. Here's how to find the handful that genuinely work for estimating, scheduling, and client communication in the trades.

item.title: Is AI Going to Take Your Job?
item.description: The WEF projects 92 million jobs displaced by AI and 170 million created. Here's what the numbers actually mean, and who's most at risk.

item.title: Okay, So Where Do You Actually Start?
item.description: Most businesses start with the technology and work backward to the problem. Here's why that tends to go badly, and what to do instead.

item.title: What Is an AI Agent?
item.description: AI assistants answer questions. Agents handle the whole thing. Here's what that distinction means, and why one in ten small businesses is already using them.

item.title: World Models, Distillation Wars, and the Inevitable Convergence
item.description: While Western and Chinese AI labs fight over distilled model outputs, the actual next frontier requires something no single country can build alone.

item.title: The Businesses That Jumped In First Are Already Lapping the Ones Still Deciding
item.description: A Google Cloud survey of 3,400 business leaders found 74% of companies using AI are already seeing a return. What that means for Okanagan businesses.

item.title: 73% of BC Businesses Haven't Thought About AI Yet
item.description: 73% of Canadian small businesses haven't considered AI yet. Here's what the ones that have are doing with it, and what that means for Okanagan businesses.

item.title: Don't Believe Everything the Robot Says
item.description: AI sounds confident even when it's making things up. Two habits that keep you from relying on bad answers.

item.title: Five Minutes and a Free Account: Your First Real Conversation with AI
item.description: Opening your first AI account takes five minutes. Here's what to do once you're in, and how to have a conversation that's actually useful.
